thread:
yu: Heads-up: rack-12 reporting recurring PCIe AER and NVLink link flaps this morning. Noticed higher 95th/99th for a few queues.
ops-bot: Alert: AER_XID_SPIKE on rack-12 (6 GPUs) — paging @sre-oncall
chen: paste the dmesg and nvidia-smi -q output please
yu: dmesg snippets:
```
[ 98765.432101] pcieport 0000:04:00.0: AER: Multiple Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error received
[ 98765.432108] NVRM: Xid (0000:04:00): 43, pid=0, fault: channel exception
[ 98765.733333] NVIDIA: GPU 0000:04:00.0: NVLink error counter: link0=18 link2=21
[ 98765.733340] NVRM: GPU reset succeeded
```
and nvlink counters are incrementing on slot 04:00 and 04:80
maria: Xid 43 + NVLink counters that big are ugly. Are these ECC corrected spikes as well or just UCEs?
aj: impact: two hyperparam sweeps saw checkpoint uploads fail momentarily and one realtime embedder got 2s tail spikes
yu: ECC corrected errors rose from ~0 to ~240/min on GPU 4 in the window. No persistent CUDA OOMs.
infra-bot: Inventory check: affected nodes g12-01..g12-06. Riser vendor=Foxconn on g12-01,g12-03,g12-05; other nodes have Foxconn or generic. BIOS on g12 nodes: 2.38 (canary nodes on 2.46)
chen: collect lspci -vvv for slots 04:00/04:80 and run nvlinkErrorCounter collector for last 6h. Also get VBIOS (nvidia-smi -q -d SUPPORTED_CLOCKS | grep VBIOS) and `nvidia-bug-report.sh`
yu: running bug report now. planning a hot-swap test: move GPU from g12-01 slot04:00 -> g12-10 slot08:00 and see if errors follow card or stay with slot
sre-oncall: capacity note: rack-12 is 72 GPUs, we can spare 8 for rolling investigation. Prefer draining one node at a time. If >50% of cards on a riser vendor show errors we escalate to RMA
maria: hypothesis tree: 1) bad GPU hw (firmware drift) 2) riser/slot electrical problem 3) BIOS mismatch causing NVLink timing issues 4) intermittent cabling (if PCIe passive riser)
aj: cost/ops tradeoff: migrating priority jobs to rack-4 adds ~8% checkpoint egress and ~3ms avg latency increase due to cross-rack fabric, but avoids potential recurring resets
chen: can you run stress test (cuda-memtest + nvlink diag) on suspect card in a canary slot after moving? record logs and timestamps
yu: done the swap. errors moved with the card to g12-10. NVLink counters are now high on g12-10:04:00. Looks card-specific so far.
infra-bot: note: node g12-01 cordoned by yu at 1856791325; drain started
chen: open RMA with vendor (include NVRM logs, dmesg, nvlink counters, VBIOS and lspci). If vendor confirms card defect, get expedited replacement for 3 cards with >100 UCEs in 24h
aj: meanwhile I'll schedule migration for the two critical runs to rack-4; will update patch notes on the job run page
sre-oncall: also link perf traces to the error timeline: add distributed tracing spans around checkpointing and embed RPCs for easier correlation
maria: action list:
- yu: upload nvidia-bug-report.tar.gz for the 6 suspect GPUs to s3://redwood-diagnostics/rack12/1856791200 and flag GH issue
- chen: file RMA (Ticket#RMA-8802) and include VBIOS/BIOS info; ask vendor about known NVLink firmware advisories
- aj: migrate high-priority jobs off rack-12 until at least 3 suspect cards replaced
- infra: run 48h nvlink+ECC counter collection and collect slot-level lspci identifiers (vendor/device/subsystem)
- sre-oncall: correlate traces and confirm whether CPU-side retries align with GPU resets
yu: uploaded tarball and logs at 1856791600 to S3 path above. Marked nodes drained and placed replacement cards on standby
chen: vendor replied: asked for `nvidia-bug-report` and dmesg, requested to test with latest VBIOS if RMA not immediate. Also asked whether riser vendor repeats (foxconn appears on 3/6)
maria: if RMA slow, plan B = run BIOS 2.46 on a canary node with one suspect card to see if timing improves (schedule in next maintenance window)
aj: approved migration complete. checkpoint egress cost ~+6% for these runs, nothing material to customer SLA.
ops-bot: RMA ticket created by chen at 1856792000 — Ticket#RMA-8802
sre-oncall: follow-up: if RMA returns cards replaced, we'll run 7-day monitor for recurrence and close thread then. Keep updates concise here.
chen: closing loop: if errors follow card -> RMA, if errors stay on slot -> hardware/chassis team for riser/cabling investigation
maria: thanks all. :thumbsup: will ping infra-hardware if riser count >4 nodes
yu: will post final status when replacements installed or behavior stabilizes
ops-bot: Thread closed automatically after 7 days of inactivity (note generated at 1856792780)
